question: What is the typical duration of the postpartum period known as the puerperium?
explanation: The puerperium generally lasts for about six weeks after childbirth, which is the time required for maternal organs to return close to their pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: Why is nursing care during the puerperium so important for a new mother?

options.A: It ensures the mother avoids all postpartum sadness
options.B: It prevents sudden complications like hemorrhage and infection
options.C: It eliminates the need for any follow-up doctor visits
options.D: It guarantees the infant will sleep through the night

explanation: You've got this! Regular checks in the postpartum period help catch physical problems early, keeping the new mother safe and healthy during her recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h1)

question: What do we call the process where the uterus shrinks back to its normal, non-pregnant size?
explanation: Great job! Involution is just the medical term for the uterus quickly returning to its pre-pregnant state through steady contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h2)

question: You feel a patient's uterus (fundus) on her second day after birth and notice it feels soft and is higher than expected. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.B: Massage the fundus gently until it becomes firm
options.D: Document that the uterus is healing normally

explanation: A soft or 'boggy' uterus needs a little help! Massaging it gently makes the muscle fibers tighten up, which stops heavy bleeding. You're doing great. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h2)

question: In the popular BUBBLE-EE postpartum assessment guide, what does the second 'B' stand for?
explanation: Remember the checklist: Breasts, Uterus, Bowel, Bladder, Lochia, Episiotomy, Extremities, and Emotions. You'll master this assessment in no time! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h3)

question: Why is checking the bladder so important in the first few hours after childbirth?

options.A: Urinary retention always leads to permanent kidney failure
options.B: A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place and causes heavy bleeding
options.C: Bladder fullness is the primary sign of postpartum preeclampsia
options.D: It prevents the lochia from changing from red to white

explanation: Think of it this way: a full bladder takes up space and pushes against the uterus, stopping it from contracting properly. Keeping the bladder empty keeps mom safe from extra bleeding! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h3)

question: Why do nurses apply an ice pack to the perineum right after a vaginal delivery?

options.A: To speed up the return of lochia alba
options.B: To reduce localized swelling and numb pain
options.C: To prevent the uterus from becoming boggy

explanation: Ice is wonderful here! It narrows the blood vessels, which quickly brings down swelling and helps numb the area so the mother feels more comfortable. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h4)

question: Why do mothers who have given birth before (multiparous women) often feel stronger afterpains than first-time mothers?

options.A: Their perineal wounds are always surgically larger
options.B: They are more sensitive to standard doses of analgesics
options.C: They produce significantly less lochia than primiparous mothers
options.D: Their uterine muscles lose tone and contract intermittently with greater force

explanation: Because her uterus has worked before, it doesn't stay clamped down all at once. Instead, it relaxes and contracts rhythmically, leading to stronger cramps as it gets back into shape. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h4)

question: What direction should you teach a new mother to clean her perineal area?
explanation: Always front to back! This simple habit stops germs from the anal area from spreading to the healing vaginal and urinary openings. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h5)

question: What is the main reason we tell postpartum mothers to drink plenty of fluids and eat high-fiber foods?

options.B: To turn lochia serosa into lochia rubra
options.C: To shrink the size of the bladder

explanation: Straining after delivery can be very painful, especially with stitches or piles (hemorrhoids). Fluids and fiber keep things soft and easy! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h5)

question: What is the maximum expected duration for normal postpartum blues before they should resolve?
explanation: Postpartum blues typically peak around the fourth or fifth day and resolve spontaneously within the first two weeks after delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h6)

question: On day four after delivery, a breastfeeding mother tells you she feels overwhelmed and cries easily when the baby fusses, but she loves holding her baby and sleeps well when the baby sleeps. What is your best response?

options.A: Inform her that she shows classic signs of postpartum psychosis
options.B: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately to stabilize her hormones
options.C: Reassure her that these feelings are common postpartum blues and will likely pass soon
options.D: Immediately arrange an emergency psychiatric admission for depression

explanation: Tearfulness and mood swings in the first two weeks are totally normal 'baby blues.' A listening ear and gentle reassurance work wonders here! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h6)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of mastitis in a breastfeeding mother?

options.B: Localized breast redness, pain, and fever

explanation: Mastitis means the breast tissue is inflamed or infected. You'll usually spot a painful, red, warm area on the breast along with fever and body aches. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h7)

question: On her third day after delivery, a patient complains that her right calf is painful, swollen, and feels warmer than the left. What is the most important thing you should do?

options.A: Encourage her to walk briskly around the hospital corridor
options.B: Massage the calf firmly to break up any muscle cramps
options.C: Apply an ice pack directly to the painful calf muscle
options.D: Instruct the patient to stay off her feet and notify the physician immediately

explanation: This sounds like a deep vein thrombosis (blood clot). Never massage a suspected clot, as it could break loose and travel to the lungs—always keep the patient resting and call the doctor right away! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h7)

question: What do we call the thick, yellowish first milk produced right after birth?
explanation: Colostrum is like liquid gold for the baby! It's packed with antibodies and nutrients to protect the newborn against early infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h8)

question: What is one of the biggest benefits of placing a newborn directly on the mother's bare chest (skin-to-skin contact) right after birth?

options.A: It helps stabilize the infant's temperature and blood sugar
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing afterpains
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of newborn jaundice
options.D: It guarantees the infant will latch without any assistance

explanation: Skin-to-skin is magical! The mother's body acts like a natural incubator, helping the baby's breathing, temperature, and blood sugar stay steady. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h8)

question: Why is family planning counseling so important before a mother is discharged from the postpartum ward?

options.A: Ovulation can occur before the first postpartum menstrual period returns
options.B: Sexual intercourse is strictly forbidden for a full year
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop lochia flow
options.D: Pregnancy is impossible during the first six months postpartum

explanation: Many women are surprised to learn that an egg can be released (ovulation) before their monthly period ever comes back. Early advice helps them plan safely! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h9)

question: Which report from a postpartum mother at home means she needs to see a doctor urgently?

options.A: Experiencing mild fatigue in the late afternoon
options.B: Having pinkish-brown lochia on day ten
options.C: Soaking through more than one sanitary pad in an hour
options.D: Feeling mild muscle soreness from walking

explanation: Soaking a pad or more every single hour is a major warning sign of late postpartum hemorrhage. She needs immediate medical attention! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h9)
